The Kano State Commissioner for Information, Sanusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, has dismissed reports of an attack on the convoy of former governor Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso in Bichi Local Government Area, describing the incident as fictitious. Tofa made the comment in a post on his personal Facebook page on Sunday, accusing the Kwankwasiyya movement of fabricating the reported attack in Bichi Local Government Area of the state. “In an attempt to generate public sympathy, the Kwankwasiyya team have framed themselves a fictitious attack in Bichi, no pictures, no videos,” he wrote. The commissioner’s reaction followed reports that suspected political thugs attacked Kwankwaso’s convoy and that of the NDC governorship candidate in Kano, Aminu Abdussalam Gwarzo, during a campaign visit to Bichi on Sunday. The spokesperson for Gwarzo’s campaign, Ibrahim Garba Shu’aibu, said the team had earlier visited Tofa, Rimingado, Kabo, Gwarzo, Shanono and Bagwai local government areas without disruption before proceeding to Bichi, according to Premium Times. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources He said the team received information that some people opposed to the campaign had blocked the road leading to the area. According to him, the convoy encountered stone-throwing upon arrival, before some armed youths reportedly emerged near the Bichi Local Government Secretariat and attacked the vehicles. Shu’aibu alleged that several members of the campaign team sustained injuries, while about seven vehicles were vandalised during the incident. Obi to publish Anambra achievements in 10-day series 2027: NDC will resist attacks with equal force – Aisha Yesufu Kwankwaso’s convoy attacked in Kano – Obi The alleged attack also attracted a reaction from the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, who condemned the incident and called on security agencies to investigate and arrest those responsible. In a statement shared on his X account on Monday, Obi said several members of Kwankwaso’s entourage were reportedly injured and about seven vehicles vandalised. He described the incident as unacceptable, stressing that political differences should not justify violence, intimidation or destruction of property. Obi also urged the police and other security agencies to identify those involved, including anyone suspected of sponsoring the attack, and ensure they were brought to justice. The Kano State Police Command had yet to publicly comment on the reported incident as of the time of filing this report. Christabel Ndoeche
